tier_reason: The kitex-benchmark README GRPC section links the raw data, and scripts/reports/grpc.csv has Kitex (gRPC transport) at 193970.54 QPS against grpc-go at 114054.24 QPS at c=1000 with a 1KB echo. The code is public (grpc/kitex/, grpc/grpc/ using google.golang.org/grpc, scripts/benchmark_grpc.sh, scripts/build_grpc.sh with plain `go build -v`), and the README states the Go version (1.17.2) and CPU (Xeon Gold 5118). Code, compiler, flags and CPU are all stated, so I upgraded C to A. This follows the earlier plain-`go build` precedent.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 1.70x higher QPS than grpc-go at concurrency=1000 (193,970.54 vs 114,054.24 QPS, 1KB echo); 1.51x at concurrency=100 (156,167.24 vs 103,178.46 QPS) (derived from page data: scripts/reports/grpc.csv linked from the README)
corrections.hardware: Intel Xeon Gold 5118 @ 2.30GHz; server pinned to 4 CPUs, client to 16 CPUs (taskset/numactl) on the same host over loopback; OS Debian, kernel 5.4.56.bsk.1-amd64
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Go 1.17.2; plain `go build -v` (default flags) per scripts/build_grpc.sh. The published data commit 251be0c (2022-08-26) pins kitex v0.3.5-0.20220819080849-d19ff0111efa and google.golang.org/grpc v1.42.0
corrections.caveats: The published numbers date from 2022-08 (commit 251be0c) and use kitex v0.3.5-pre against grpc-go v1.42.0 with Go 1.17.2. The current go.mod pins kitex v0.14.1 and grpc v1.66.2, and the README data has not been refreshed since. Client and server share one host over loopback, and the README itself warns that ksoftirqd threads escape taskset. The client pools also differ: Kitex uses a gRPC connection pool of 6, and grpc-go uses the runner default of 10 connections. The benchmark is first-party.

notes: The record said CPU, OS and Go version were not stated, but the README Specification section states all three. The exact QPS values sit in scripts/reports/grpc.csv, so no chart reading is needed, and the record's approximate numbers match.
